name: PageTally – Content Inventory & Checkup
author: bryanbyfield

sections.description:
PageTally is a content inventory for your WordPress site. It scans published posts and pages and puts every issue in one sortable, filterable table under Tools → PageTally.

Use it when you need to:

  • Audit outdated content. See how long it has been since each post or page was last updated, and flag anything older than your threshold as stale.
  • Find thin content. Word counts are listed for every item. Anything under your threshold is flagged as thin.
  • Find orphaned pages and posts. PageTally counts inbound internal links from other scanned posts and pages. Zero means the item is orphaned and hard for visitors and search engines to find from your content.
  • Check featured images and alt text. Flag posts that should have a featured image and don’t, and count images in the content that are missing alt text.
  • Hunt leftover shortcodes. After you remove a plugin, leftover tags often print as raw [brackets] on the front end. PageTally lists shortcode tags that no active plugin or theme still handles.
  • Export a content plan. Filter the list, then download exactly what you are looking at as CSV.

For every published post and page the report records last modified date, word count, inbound internal links, featured image status, images missing alt text, leftover shortcodes, and a summary of issues.

How it works

  • On demand. Nothing runs until you click Run scan.
  • In batches. The scan runs in small batches from your browser, so large sites don’t hit PHP time limits. If you leave the page you can resume where it stopped.
  • Private. PageTally reads your own database. It makes no external requests, loads nothing from other sites and collects no data.
  • Filter and sort. Jump to one issue type, filter by post type, search titles and sort by any column.
  • Your thresholds. Set what counts as stale and thin under Settings → PageTally.

What it does not do

PageTally reports. It never edits, deletes or redirects content.

Internal links are counted from post and page content only. Links in menus, widgets and theme templates are not counted, and your front page and posts page are never flagged as orphaned.

For developers

PageTally has actions and filters to extend it: which post types and statuses are scanned, item data, report columns, bulk actions, CSV columns, settings fields, and events when a scan starts, when an item is scanned, and when a scan completes. All hook names start with pagetally_.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate PageTally from Plugins → Add New, or upload the pagetally folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Go to Tools → PageTally and click Run scan.
  3. Optional: adjust thresholds under Settings → PageTally.
sections.faq:
Will scanning slow down my site?

Scans only run while you have the PageTally screen open. Each request handles a small batch (25 posts by default, adjustable) and stops early if a batch runs long.

Who can see the report?

Only users who can manage options (administrators by default).

Why is a shortcode flagged that I know works?

PageTally flags tags that no plugin or theme has registered when the scan runs. A few plugins only register their shortcodes on the front end. If you see a false positive, please open a support topic. Developers can use the pagetally_ignored_shortcodes filter.

Why is a post with links pointing to it shown as orphaned?

Only links inside published post and page content are counted. Links from menus, widgets, theme templates or other post types are not. Links to drafts and to external sites are also ignored. The front page and the posts page are never flagged as orphaned.

Does it count images without alt text added by blocks or page builders?

It checks <img> tags saved in the post content, which covers the block editor and the classic editor. Images a page builder renders from its own data at display time are not checked.

Can I change what counts as stale or thin?

Yes. Under Settings → PageTally you set the stale age in days (default 365) and the thin-content word count (default 300). Threshold changes apply to the report straight away. The setting that treats alt="" as missing applies on the next scan.

Does it delete anything on uninstall?

Deleting the plugin removes its two database tables and its options. Your content is never changed.
